owner: CC (code+proofs); Akien (the design ruling: one ticket both halves, post-build inspector NOT an overnight scan, 2026-07-29)
intention: WORK NEVER RIDES LOOSE — durability becomes physics at TWO EVENTS and no clock. (1) THE CROSSING: a new build_inspector FILTER (`working_tree_clean`) reds a component whose own subtree carries uncommitted changes, so a stone cannot be promoted out of PROVEME while the code it claims exists only in a working tree. (2) THE BOUNDARY: /saveslate stops being hand-authored JSON and gets a write door that measures both roots by instrument, makes any dirt durable (commit + push) BEFORE writing the slate, and records the resulting shas in the slate itself — so a continuity record can never outlive the work it describes.
why: The durability gate has been a bound, unbuilt gate since 2026-07-15: node_classes/code-seam.json `extra_gates` reads 'a code-seam is not done until tested AND durably committed (git). Durability-of-stones sits on the emit chokepoint (physics), not a step anyone remembers to run.' skills/commit/intention+why.json says the same from the other side: 'a skill invented to force a behavior is policy standing in for a missing gate.' Both have been pointing at this stone for two weeks. Today it came due from the far end: /saveslate wrote slate 2026-07-29-resume-opus-inline while SEVEN files of stone C's berth-work sat uncommitted in cairn and one in CairnCommons. The slate named the dirty files honestly and was still the wrong artifact — a durable record whose pointer resolved to a working tree, which a dead box resolves to nothing. That is Law 1's most expensive failure: not re-deriving a settled answer, but re-deriving a BUILT one. build_inspector's own growth rule already claims this case in its charter: 'a failure Akien catches that a filter could have caught becomes a filter, and the class stops recurring.' Akien caught it. A filter could have caught it.
traces_to: Law 4 — the whole point: 'commit before you stop' in an operator's habit is policy; a filter at the crossing and a door at the boundary are physics. This stone discharges the durability IOU named in code-seam.json extra_gates and skills/commit/intention+why.json, both dated 2026-07-15
Law 1 — uncommitted proven work that must be rebuilt is re-deriving the SETTLED at its most expensive; the defect Law 1 exists to stop
Law 3 — the slate's own charter says 'a slate that names a file is a pointer to verify, not a proof'; a sha IS checkable, so the durability field turns that line from hypothesis into measurement
Law 8 — a stone promoted with its code only in a working tree is a hollow pass: the proof ran against bytes nothing durable holds

the founding intention (get Akien out of running the system) — 'commit when Akien has asked' put him back in the operator seat; the asymmetry is the argument: an unnecessary commit costs a line of history, an uncommitted one can cost the work
state: code-seam@v1: THINKME -> [TICKETME] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> LEARNME -> PROVED   (cast 2026-07-29; leaf, so TICKETME is skippable per the class's skippable_summons; chart pending — the entry gate demands a berthed chart chain before BUILDME)
gates: proof gate: teeth beside the code, under the tester with the netns seal. THE CROSSING HALF (cairn/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py): the new filter fires on a synthetic component with seeded dirt and stays quiet on a clean one (tooth 1 + tooth 2, the founding fire-and-stay-quiet pair); it carries its seeding failure as docstring Provenance (tooth 10 refuses a filter nobody was taught by); inspector.py gains no forbidden import (tooth 12 — `subprocess` is legal, the forbidden set is network + the `deepen` oracle, VERIFIED by reading the tooth, and git status survives the netns seal because it is local); every existing tooth still greens. Live gate: the filter fires in anger at a real PROVEME exit with real dirt, and the history stays untouched on the refusal. THE BOUNDARY HALF (skills/saveslate/proofs/): a dirty tree in BOTH roots, fired through the door, leaves both roots clean and pushed and the slate carrying two shas that resolve to commits containing exactly that dirt; a slate written with a wrong template key refuses (which retires the live `at_sea`/`in_flight` drift below as a consequence, not a second fix); the door NEVER refuses to write a slate — see falsifier.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a clean component draws the new finding (a gate that always fires gets unwired — build_inspector's own tooth 1); (2) seeded dirt fails to red the crossing; (3) the boundary door REFUSES to write a slate on a dirty tree — refusing is the wrong direction: the door commits, it never blocks; (4) the door silently absorbs an untracked file it cannot account for (see the publish constraint in dependencies); (5) a slate lands whose recorded shas do not resolve, or resolve to commits missing the dirt they claim; (6) anything in this stone acquires a clock. THE COMMIT DIRECTION IS RATIFIED (Akien 2026-07-29, resolving the one open assumption in this cast): the 2026-07-29 stop was NOT a deliberate resting state — 'if I didn't stop it when I did, it would have run out of usage within a couple of moments, and it'd be hard stopped then. so if that's the cause of those files, then it had work in progress we should finish.' A dirty tree at a boundary therefore means INTERRUPTED WORK, not preserved work, and the door's job is wider than durability alone: the dirt is a SIGNAL that a voyage is mid-flight, so the slate should derive what is still owed from it rather than depend on a human writing that prose. Retained as a falsifier only in the narrow form: if a future dirty-at-boundary is ever genuinely a raw state Akien wants untouched, the door needs an explicit opt-out, not a reversal.
horizon: re-read when: a third durability event appears (the pattern would then earn a shared shape rather than two sites); the tester lands and the hand-run VALIDATION becomes automatic; CLAUDE.md's 'Rules awaiting physics' section is next edited — the durability IOU is NOT currently listed there (it lives in code-seam.json extra_gates + the /commit charter), and this stone landing is the moment to decide whether that section should have carried it all along.

PREREQUISITE MEASURED FALSE 2026-07-29, at ticket skills-ride-the-chokepoint's close: build_inspector's census is scoped to cairn/ and CANNOT SEE skills/ AT ALL. Inspecting the sail address refuses — 'no component skills/sail under <root>/cairn — the census sees [base, build_inspector, bus, chart, ...]'. So the crossing-half filter as cast would have ZERO jurisdiction over skills/, which is exactly where the newly-crossing skill class lives, AND over anything else outside cairn/. Two consequences: (1) the crossing half covers strictly less than this ticket assumed at cast, so the boundary half carries more of the load than stated; (2) widening orient's device_census is either a dependency of this stone or a sibling stone in front of it — Akien's call, and it must be settled at constrain, not discovered at build. Do not build the filter believing it covers skills/.

CairnCommons/slates/_charter+why.json — becomes the schema the door validates. NOTE A LIVE DRIFT, AND A CORRECTION TO THIS TICKET'S FIRST DRAFT: I wrote 'its template names the key `in_flight`, every real slate writes `at_sea`'. MEASURED 2026-07-29 at the /sorted pivot the same day — THE CENSUS RUNS THE OTHER WAY: 29 slates write `in_flight` (the template's own key), 6 write `at_sea`, and the `at_sea` ones are the RECENT drift, following skills/saveslate/SKILL.md's prose rather than the template. So the divergence is SKILL.md vs the template, not the slates vs the template. The charter's claim that 'the single commons emit chokepoint validates every record against the template below' is the real defect — that validation demonstrably does not fire, which is why a prose file could quietly out-vote the schema for six slates. AKIEN'S RULING WANTED BEFORE THE DOOR PICKS A SIDE, because cheap and right may differ: `in_flight` holds the numbers and the schema, but `at_sea` is the domain-correct term for a system of voyages, harbors and berths ([[build-to-the-tool-naming]] — 'in flight' is aviation, and a term should be derivable from its native domain). Whichever wins, the door validating at all is what retires this note

PUBLISH CONSTRAINT (bounded, not eliminated): both roots are public on github.com/akienm, so the boundary door's push is an outward act. Bounded BY THE THREE-ROOTS LAW — class-space holds nothing private by construction; credentials, logs and instance state live in ~/.cairn. Residual risk is a stray scratch file, so the door must NAME every untracked file it absorbs in the slate rather than sweeping silently. Push is required, not optional: a local-only commit still dies with the box

But stone C spanned cairn/base AND skills/sail, so a per-component filter crossing one of them is blind to dirt in the other. The residue it cannot see — non-component paths (MAP.md, CLAUDE.md, top-level) and cross-component dirt — is the boundary door's jurisdiction, and the boundary is never fired if a session simply ends. THE COVER FOR THAT RESIDUE IS ON-READ, NOT A CLOCK: /loadslate measures both roots and reports before restoring, which is exactly how this bug surfaced by hand this session. Bounding the loss window by 'next time anyone touches the system' is the same window in which the work matters
